seo.metaTitle: Los Gatos Medical Malpractice Help | Free Case Review
seo.metaDescription: Hurt by a medical error in Los Gatos? Get a free case review from an attorney who handles malpractice claims. No fee unless you recover.

hero.subtitle: If a diagnosis, surgery, or treatment went wrong at a Los Gatos or Santa Clara County medical facility, our team can review your case and explain where you stand under California's malpractice law. There's no cost to find out if you have a claim.

about.title: Los Gatos Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in Los Gatos often involve patients treated at local clinics or nearby Santa Clara County hospitals who left with an injury that shouldn't have happened. Maybe a scan was misread, a medication dose was wrong, or a surgical step was skipped. California law doesn't make these cases easy — a bad result by itself isn't enough, and the law requires a qualified medical expert to explain how the care fell below the accepted standard. Strict notice and filing deadlines also apply, so timing matters from the start. Our team reviews medical records, consults with appropriate experts, and explains whether a case is worth pursuing — all before any commitment or cost to you.

items.title: Deadlines Are Tight and Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from when it happened, and a 90-day notice must go out before any lawsuit is filed. Missing these windows can end a case before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Required, Not Optional
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to establish that care fell below the accepted standard. Our team knows how to find and work with the right expert.

items.title: Damages Caps Are Complex and Changing
items.desc: California caps non-economic damages, but that cap rises each year under current law. We can walk you through how that cap and the case specifics might affect your situation.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't prove malpractice. There has to be evidence that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why a qualified expert review is almost always required.

items.question: Does Los Gatos being a smaller city affect where my treatment happened?
items.answer: Many Los Gatos residents are treated at larger Santa Clara County facilities outside city limits, and that's fine — what matters is where the care occurred and when you discovered the problem. We can sort out the right jurisdiction and deadlines regardless of which facility was involved.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk with us about your case?
items.answer: Nothing. Our consultation is free, and we generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You can ask questions and get clarity before deciding anything.
